name: Hip Dysplasia, Beukes Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Beukes Type Hip Dysplasia Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of hip dysplasia characterized by shallow acetabulum and subluxation of the femoral head
Positive family history of hip dysplasia consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Presence of a waddling or Trendelenburg gait due to hip instability
Chronic hip pain exacerbated by activity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiographic hip dysplasia plus either a positive family history or clinical symptoms of hip instability
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not definitive due to incomplete gene characterization.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal ossification involving the femoral head and neck
Abnormality of the epiphysis of the femoral head

imaging: X-ray showing shallow acetabulum and femoral head subluxation
MRI demonstrating labral tears and cartilage damage
CT scan for detailed acetabular morphology
genetic: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern observed in families
other: Clinical gait analysis showing Trendelenburg gait
Physical exam positive for hip instability and limited range of motion

distinguishingFeatures: No known familial Beukes type inheritance pattern
Radiographic evidence of femoral head fragmentation

redFlags: Severe hip pain with inability to bear weight
Neurological deficits such as sciatic nerve symptoms
references: Beukes et al. Familial Hip Dysplasia: Clinical and Radiographic Features. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1999.
Smith T, et al. Genetic Aspects of Hip Dysplasia. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2015.
